title: Death March to the Parallel World Rhapsody
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ichiro Suzuki, an overworked 29-year-old game programmer, falls asleep during crunch time and wakes in a fantasy world as 15-year-old 'Satou', with a game menu in his head. A panicked area attack wipes out a lizardman army (and accidentally a god), leaving him hugely overpowered. He hides his level and travels the world as a merchant and sightseer, gathering a party of rescued slave girls, an elf and a homunculus. Manga adaptation of a web-born light novel.
life_message: A good life is a calm one: travel, good food and quietly using great power to look after the people who join you.

content.note: Fantasy battles with lizardmen, demons and an undead king; a mass 'Meteor' attack wipes out an army (Wikipedia plot; AniList Demons, Dungeon; MU Godly Powers). Detail level to verify.
Dungeon peril and demons; the undead king's backstory involves murder and execution of his family (Wikipedia).

Female harem: several girls, including 10-11-year-old party members, have crushes on Satou (Wikipedia, AniList Female Harem). MU lists Ecchi and sexually experienced male lead; MangaDex 'safe' (to verify).
Inn and town life; none tagged (to verify).
Opens on programmer burnout from 'death march' overwork; slaves' prior abuse (AniList Bullying, low rank).
Satou buys slaves (Arisa, Lulu) and keeps them as party members, framed as rescue; a geas prevents freeing them (Wikipedia; AniList and MU Slavery).
MMORPG menus, levels and skill points structure the story (MU Game Elements, Level System).

dominant: Pragmatic overpowered hero; found-family party; leisure and sightseeing

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Satou avoids fights and hides his strength; he fights to protect his party rather than to answer insults.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Satou chooses not to be tied to any one place and wanders the world as he likes (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: His loyalty centers on his party, a found family of rescued girls.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Master-slave bonds, nobles and a hereditary knighthood are accepted parts of the world.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Game logic, menus and calculation guide choices; gods exist but are not worshipped by him.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Leisure, food and sightseeing are the goal once safety is secured.

folkways.japan: The isekai premise grew from Japanese web-novel culture (Shosetsuka ni Naro), and the title names the 'death march' crunch of Japanese software work, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: No review or summary in the sources describes delivery; style inferred from premise and tags (to verify).
delivery.note: The calm-life ideal is carried by Satou's travels; the world's slavery is not questioned in the summaries.

winners_losers: Satou and the girls he gathers win steadily; a corrupt priest and an undead king lose. Sympathy goes to the calm, competent protector rather than to questioning the world's slavery.
